s1
Meet ThaliSense: an A.I. nutrition and metabolic-health coach, built for Indian meals, that runs entirely on your phone.
s2

India has a hundred and one million people living with diabetes, and a hundred and thirty-six million more with prediabetes. Most of it is driven by everyday food. But calorie apps don't know pesarattu or kadhi, they use Western B.M.I. cut-offs that miss South Asian risk, and they want your health data on their servers.
s3

Here's the live app. I'll load a demo week for Priya: thirty-eight, from Chennai, vegetarian, with a parent who has diabetes. Today tracks her calories and nutrients against personal targets, and every meal gets a plate score for how balanced it is.
s4

Logging is natural. Type it the way you'd say it: two chapathi, dal, and half a cup of curd. The parser understands quantities, Hindi and Tamil number words, regional names and typos, across a hundred and eight Indian dishes.
s5

Or snap the whole thali. A vision model fine-tuned for Indian food runs right here in the browser. It scans every part of the plate, and finds the samosa, jalebi, dhokla and pav bhaji. The photo never leaves the phone.
s6

Now the coach. This agent works like a dietitian, and it shows every step. It assesses her risk, reviews her week, and finds the patterns: too many calories, about sixty percent of energy from carbohydrate, and sweet coffee through the day. Then it suggests swaps for foods she already eats, with the weekly impact of each one.
s7

It drafts a seven-day South Indian vegetarian plan within her two-hundred-rupee budget, checks every day against her targets, and repairs the misses with real portions. She can log any meal with one tap, or share the week on WhatsApp.
s8
Her Indian Diabetes Risk Score is eighty, in the high-risk range, so ThaliSense tells her to get a blood test. Weekly weight and waist entries show her progress: down two point four kilos so far.
s9

And we measured it. On one thousand six hundred and ninety-four test photos, our fine-tuned model names the dish correctly eighty-eight percent of the time, and ninety-five percent within its top three, up from seventy-one percent for standard CLIP.
ThaliSense. Private, offline, and installable. Eat the food you love, and know what it does to you. Try it at thalisense dot vercel dot app.
